name: The Common Paper
summary: A local editorial identity whose authority comes from readable reporting, visible attribution and the familiar rhythm of a newspaper.

palette.name: Background
palette.evidence: Native Office page/sheet white ground; explicit design choice retaining the reading surface.

palette.name: Text
palette.evidence: used style Normal explicit text color

palette.name: Table header
palette.evidence: Native reference.docx word/document.xml active shading/border value #202020; source visual and native-design-style-audit corroboration.

typography.usage: Titles and short section openings; source used style Heading3.
Reading text, supporting labels and detailed explanations; source used style NewsDeck.

recognitionRules: Use the full serif masthead above a ruled issue line.
Separate stories with columns, subheads and captions rather than rounded cards.
Keep black-and-white reproduction as a first-class edition.
Distinguish headlines, reported text and editorial notes through type and spacing.

principles: Make the invitation warm and the practical details exact.
Use the identity’s sample as a rhythm and vocabulary reference, not as a factual project claim.
voice.sample: A shared place deserves a paper with room for more than one voice.
voice.sampleStatus: Original fictional brand copy authored for this guide, not a quotation or factual claim.
avoid: Avoid speaking for an entire community or implying confirmed attendance.
Avoid invented testimonials, performance claims and quotation attribution.
voice.secondaryExample: Come for the part that interests you; here is what to expect.
voice.cadence: Short opening, concrete follow-through; vary sentence length for explanation.

logoDirection: Use THE COMMON PAPER as a Baskerville or source serif masthead with paired rules. No separate logo symbol.
invariants: Use the full serif masthead above a ruled issue line.
Separate stories with columns, subheads and captions rather than rounded cards.
Keep black-and-white reproduction as a first-class edition.
adaptations: A digital issue can stack columns while retaining story order and bylines.
A single-sheet edition keeps one strong lead story.
Keep the full name with any new symbol until the audience can recognize it independently.

fonts.sourceFontDependency: Baskerville is a separately licensed/system font; not bundled.
Georgia is a separately licensed Microsoft/system font; not bundled.

clearSpaceRule: Keep one half of the main wordmark cap height clear around the full silhouette, including its source-derived supporting device.

minimumSize.status: production minimum based on rendered 220/180px wordmark and 32/64px symbol inspection; verify again for unusual substrates
